The one rare ingredient is an **8-bit operand** (`int8`/`fp8_e5m2`): every 8-bit case in [`testing/python/tilelibrary/test_tilelang_tilelibrary_gemm_sp.py`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/testing/python/tilelibrary/test_tilelang_tilelibrary_gemm_sp.py) uses `K == block_K` (single K-block: `(128,128,64,block_K=64)` int8, `(64,128,128,block_K=128)` int8, `(128,128,64,block_K=64)` fp8_e5m2), the only multi-K rows are `float16`/`bfloat16`, and the shipped example is `matmul_sp_fp16` (fp16-only). So the 8-bit × (`K > block_K`) intersection is exercised nowhere in examples or tests, which is why CI is green.

**Example-run result (this session, 0.1.13, v0.1.13 `examples/gemm_sp/`).** I ran the shipped `example_gemm_sp.py` verbatim. Its default 1024³ config compiles cleanly (no `ThreadSync` abort) but fails at *runtime* on sm_89 with `Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 167936` — an sm_89 SMEM-capacity limit, unrelated to this ICE. Re-run on a config that fits sm_89 (`--m 256 --n 256 --k 256 --block_M 128 --block_N 128 --block_K 64 --num_stages 1`, 4 K-iterations, multi-K) it **compiles and passes precision** (`Precision check passed. diff: 0.00158`). So the shipped example **dodges this bug because it is fp16** (16-bit metadata layout, group=32/interweave=4), not because it avoids the multi-K loop — a multi-K fp16 sparse GEMM is exactly what it exercises and it works. The bug requires the 8-bit-operand metadata layout, which no shipped example or test uses together with `K > block_K`.

Adjacent configurations tested this session on sm_89 (0.1.13), each in a fresh process/cache (see §17 for the full 4-axis sweep):

| config | K / block_K | K-iters | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| int8 sparse (trigger) | 256 / 128 | 2 | `Cannot match type int32 vs handle` |
| int8 sparse | 256 / 64 | 4 | `Cannot match type int32 vs handle` (same root) |
| **fp8_e5m2** sparse | 256 / 128 | 2 | `Cannot match type int32 vs handle` (**same root**, same frame) |
| int8 sparse, transpose_E | 256 / 128 | 2 | `Cannot match type int32 vs handle` (same root) |
| int8 sparse (control) | 256 / 256 | 1 | compiles + launches |
| **float16** sparse | 256 / 128 | 2 | **compiles** (16-bit metadata layout, no crash) |
| **dense** int8 `T.gemm` (control) | 256 / 128 | 2 | **compiles** (no sparse metadata → no crash) |
| int8 sparse, repeat-run | 256 / 128 | 2 | identical crash ×3 (deterministic ICE, not a race) |

Same-root vs distinct: all the 8-bit-operand multi-K rows (int8 and fp8_e5m2, block_K = 128 and 64, transpose_E on/off) are the **same** root — any `K > block_K` 8-bit sparse loop aborts identically in the same `Summarize`/`BinaryOpMatchTypes` frame. The non-crashing rows delimit the boundary: single-K-block int8 (no loop-var relaxation), fp16 multi-K (16-bit metadata layout), and dense int8 multi-K (no sparse metadata layout at all) all compile, isolating the defect to *8-bit-operand sparse metadata × multi-iteration K-loop*. (Separately: the single-K-block int8 sparse kernel launches but its result did not match a dense `int8→int32` reference on this sm_89 run — max abs diff 188; an unrelated int8-sparse-on-sm_89 correctness question, deliberately out of scope for this compile-abort issue.)

**Generalization (root levels + 4-axis sweep, all cells RUN this session).**

*Two-level root.*

- **SOURCE-level root** (which implementation is fragile): [`PointerAccessIsDisjoint`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/transform/thread_storage_sync.cc#L1503) forms [`lhs_max < rhs_min`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/transform/thread_storage_sync.cc#L1548) from touched-`IntSet` bounds that the per-loop handler [relaxes over the loop var via `arith::EvalSet`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/transform/thread_storage_sync.cc#L887). When `EvalSet` cannot bound the composed metadata index it returns the `±inf` sentinel (a `handle`-typed node); `<` on `int32` vs `handle` fails [`BinaryOpMatchTypes`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/8df8ebd61659505dd7005f4820b030e983e2c005/src/tirx/op/op.cc#L249). The missing guard (no `is_pos_inf`/`is_neg_inf` check before the `<`) is the true fragile site — it is generic to *any* access whose relaxed `IntSet` is unbounded.
- **OPERATOR-level root** (what correlates): the `T.gemm_sp` **8-bit-operand metadata read** — [`ldmatrix_e`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/tilelang/cuda/intrinsics/macro/mma_sp_macro_generator.py#L299) selects a `metadata_*_layout_8bit` thread→(row,col) map composed with the 32-bit-metadata `ColumnMajorInterleaved` (`group=16, interweave=2`) that [`make_cutlass_metadata_layout_sm8x`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/tilelang/layout/gemm_sp.py#L121) *forces* onto 8-bit operands ([the sm8x layout requires 32-bit metadata for `int8`/`uint8`/fp8, 16-bit for fp16/bf16](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/tilelang/layout/gemm_sp.py#L128-L132)). This 32-bit-metadata interleave is the composed index `EvalSet` gives up on; the 16-bit fp16 interleave (`group=32, interweave=4`) stays boundable.

**4-axis sweep** (each cell run in a fresh process + fresh `TILELANG_CACHE_DIR`, `K=256`, `block_M=block_N=128`, `threads=128`, `num_stages=1`; observed result recorded, not asserted):

| axis | cell tested | result | same-root? |
|---|---|---|---|
| related-type | `fp8_e5m2` a_dtype + int32 meta, block_K=128 (2 K-iters) | `Cannot match type int32 vs handle` — identical `ThreadSync`/`Summarize`/`BinaryOpMatchTypes` frame | **SAME** — bug is the 8-bit family, not int8 alone |
| related-type | `float16` a_dtype + int16 meta, block_K=128 (2 K-iters) | compiles cleanly | distinct — fp16 uses the 16-bit metadata layout that `EvalSet` can bound |
| related-type | `int8` a_dtype + **int16** meta, multi-K | `ValueError: metadata should be 32 bit, got int16` at layout build | unreachable config — sm8x forces 32-bit meta on 8-bit operands |
| related-type | `float16` a_dtype + **int32** meta, multi-K | `ValueError: metadata should be 16 bit, got int32` at layout build | unreachable config — sm8x forces 16-bit meta on fp16 (cannot cross fp16 into the crashing layout) |
| related-type | `uint8` a_dtype + int32 meta, multi-K | `KeyError: uint8` in sparse `GROUP_CONFIG` | unreachable config — uint8 is not a supported sparse operand |
| related-operator | `int8` `gemm_sp` **transpose_E=True**, block_K=128 (2 K-iters) | `Cannot match type int32 vs handle` (same frame) | **SAME** — the other `ldmatrix_e` branch still composes the same metadata index |
| related-operator | dense `int8` `T.gemm`, block_K=128 (2 K-iters) | compiles cleanly | distinct — no sparse metadata layout, so no unbounded index |
| related-source | `int8` sparse, **block_K=64** (4 K-iters) | `Cannot match type int32 vs handle` (same frame) | **SAME** — any `K > block_K` count relaxes over the loop var |

**Example-run (PART 1).** The shipped `examples/gemm_sp/example_gemm_sp.py` is fp16-only (`matmul_sp_fp16`). Run verbatim (v0.1.13 sources), it **compiles and passes precision** on a sm_89-fitting config (`--k 256 --block_K 64`, 4 K-iters, multi-K): `Precision check passed. diff: 0.00158`. Its 1024³ default compiles but hits an unrelated sm_89 SMEM-capacity runtime error (`Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 167936`). So the shipped example **dodges this bug because it is fp16, not because it avoids the multi-K loop** — it runs the multi-K loop successfully. Verified there is no shipped example or test that combines an 8-bit operand with `K > block_K`.

**Reframe.** Boundary is wider than the original int8-only framing but still bounded: the bug is the **8-bit-operand sparse family (int8 and fp8_e5m2)** — precisely the set that `make_cutlass_metadata_layout_sm8x` forces onto the 32-bit-metadata ColumnMajorInterleaved. It is *not* reachable for fp16/bf16 (different, boundable layout) nor for uint8 (unsupported operand). Title and Problem updated to "8-bit-operand". No new distinct bug was found while sweeping (the fp16/int16-meta and fp16/int32-meta `ValueError`s and the uint8 `KeyError` are input-validation guards firing correctly, not defects).

title: [BUG][Fuzzer][wrong-code] Auto-vectorized `float32` `T.atomic_add` into shared emits a global-only vector builtin and crashes at launch (sm_90)
body:
### Required prerequisites

- [x] I have searched the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues) that this hasn't already been reported.

### What version of TileLang are you using?

0.1.13 (latest release)

### System information

TileLang 0.1.13 / NVIDIA H100 (sm_90), CUDA 12.x. The launch failure requires sm_90 (the float32 vector-atomic gate) and was reproduced this session on an H100: the repro emits a `float32`-width `AtomicAddx2` on the shared buffer and aborts at launch (`InternalError`, CUDA launch failure, under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`). The sm_89 non-crash controls below were run on an L40S with TileLang 0.1.13.

### Problem description

A `T.atomic_add` of a `float32` value into a **shared-memory** destination, written inside a `T.Parallel` loop that gives each thread ≥2 elements, aborts the kernel at launch with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (`cudaErrorLaunchFailure`). The identical accumulation is correct when the same loop maps one element per thread (scalar `AtomicAdd`), and the identical vectorized code is correct when the destination is global. So the crash is the intersection of *vectorization* and *shared scope*. Not a regression — see Provenance.

Two passes interact. The `VectorizeLoop` pass picks the atomic-add width from the destination dtype and SM version only (`GetMaxAtomicVectorSize`), never the destination memory scope — for `float32` on sm_90 it returns 4, so the per-thread atomics are rewritten to the `atomic_addx2`/`atomic_addx4` intrinsic. `CodeGenCUDA` then emits `AtomicAddx2((&Bs[...]), *(float2*)(...))` / `AtomicAddx4(...)`, which resolve (in the `atomic.h` codegen-time template) to the sm≥90 `float32` overloads whose relaxed branch is the CUDA `atomicAdd(reinterpret_cast<float2*>(ref), ...)` / `float4*` builtin. Those vector overloads are defined only for the global address space; passing a shared pointer yields an illegal memory access at launch. The scalar `atomicAdd(float*)` and the `float16` vectorized `atomicAdd(half2*)` both accept shared, so only the `float32`-vectorized-into-shared case faults.

<details><summary>Trigger boundary and controls (0.1.13). The sm_90 float32-into-shared crash row was reproduced this session on an H100; the sm_89 rows were run this session on an L40S. Only the sm_90 float32-GLOBAL-destination row is inferred (not run).</summary>

| arch | dst dtype | dst scope | per-thread elems | emitted | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sm_90 | `float32` | shared | 2 | `AtomicAddx2((&Bs[..]), *(float2*)..)` | **launch failure** (`InternalError`, CUDA launch failure) (RUN, H100) |
| sm_90 | `float32` | shared | 4 | `AtomicAddx4((&Bs[..]), *(float4*)..)` | **launch failure** (inferred, same overload family) |
| sm_89 | `float32` | shared | 2 | scalar `AtomicAdd(&Bs[..], ..)` (fp32 width=1 on sm<90) | correct, maxerr 0.0 (RUN) |
| sm_89 | `float32` | shared | 1 (threads=256) | scalar `AtomicAdd(&Bs[..], ..)` | correct, maxerr 0.0 (RUN) |
| sm_89 | `float32` | **global** | 2 | scalar `AtomicAdd(&B[..], ..)` (fp32 width=1 on sm<90) | correct, maxerr 0.0 (RUN) |
| sm_89 | `float16` | shared | 2 | `AtomicAddx2((&Bs[..]), *(uint1*)..)` (→ `atomicAdd(half2*)`) | correct, maxerr 0.0 (RUN) |
| sm_89 | `bfloat16` | shared | 2 | `AtomicAddx2((&Bs[..]), *(uint1*)..)` (→ `atomicAdd(__nv_bfloat162*)`) | correct, maxerr 0.0 (RUN) |

The sm_90 float32-into-shared row was reproduced this session on an H100: the emitted `AtomicAddx2` on the shared `Bs` aborts at launch (`InternalError`, CUDA launch failure). The sm_89 rows isolate two things. First, `float32` atomic never vectorizes below sm_90 (`GetMaxAtomicVectorSize` returns 1), so the crash cannot appear there — this is why the fault is sm_90-only. Second, the `float16`/`bfloat16` vectorized-into-shared path DOES fire on sm_89 and runs clean, because its relaxed vectorized builtin (`atomicAdd(half2*)` / `atomicAdd(__nv_bfloat162*)`) accepts a shared pointer — showing the width-selection scope-blindness is shared across dtypes, but only the `float32` overloads reject shared. On sm_90 the `float32` global-destination row is expected to remain correct (same `AtomicAddx2`, global pointer is legal), isolating scope as the crash trigger; that global-destination row is the only inferred cell (not run).

</details>

### Reproducible example code

```python
# REPRO (sm_90): float32 T.atomic_add into a SHARED buffer, auto-vectorized to AtomicAddx2.
# threads=128 over 256 elements -> 2 elems/thread -> on sm_90, width-4 fp32 vectorization
# emits AtomicAddx2/x4(float2*/float4*), a global-only builtin, on a shared ptr -> launch failure.
# (On sm<90 fp32 atomic keeps width 1 -> scalar AtomicAdd -> runs clean; the crash needs sm_90.)
import torch, tilelang, tilelang.language as T

N = 256
@T.prim_func
def f(A: T.Tensor((N,), "float32"), B: T.Tensor((N,), "float32")):
    with T.Kernel(1, threads=128) as bx:
        Bs = T.alloc_shared((N,), "float32")
        for i in T.Parallel(N):
            Bs[i] = 0.0
        for i in T.Parallel(N):
            T.atomic_add(Bs[i], A[i])      # -> AtomicAddx2((&Bs[..]), *(float2*)..)
        for i in T.Parallel(N):
            B[i] = Bs[i]

k = tilelang.compile(f)
A = torch.arange(N, dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
B = torch.zeros(N, dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
k(A, B)                                    # CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
print((B - A).abs().max().item())          # never reached
```

```python
# CONTROL: identical kernel, threads=256 -> 1 elem/thread -> scalar AtomicAdd on shared.
import torch, tilelang, tilelang.language as T

N = 256
@T.prim_func
def f(A: T.Tensor((N,), "float32"), B: T.Tensor((N,), "float32")):
    with T.Kernel(1, threads=256) as bx:
        Bs = T.alloc_shared((N,), "float32")
        for i in T.Parallel(N):
            Bs[i] = 0.0
        for i in T.Parallel(N):
            T.atomic_add(Bs[i], A[i])      # -> scalar AtomicAdd(&Bs[..], ..)
        for i in T.Parallel(N):
            B[i] = Bs[i]

k = tilelang.compile(f)
A = torch.arange(N, dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
B = torch.zeros(N, dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
k(A, B)
print((B - A).abs().max().item())          # -> 0.0 (correct)
```

### Traceback

(Reproduced this session on an H100 with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`: `grid=(1,1,1) block=(128,1,1) dyn_smem_bytes=1024`, `InternalError` / CUDA launch failure.)

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
Search for `cudaErrorLaunchFailure' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information.
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
```

### Expected behavior

The `float32` shared-buffer accumulation should complete and produce the correct sum, as the scalar lowering of the same call already does (control above, maxerr 0.0) and as the `float16` vectorized path already does on shared. Shared-memory atomic add with relaxed ordering is an intended use — [#1998](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues/1998) confirms the `memory_order == relaxed` atomics go through the generic `atomicAdd(...)` builtins for exactly this.

### Additional context

**Root cause.** `VectorizeLoop` picks the `float32` atomic-add vector width from the destination dtype and SM version alone and never inspects the destination's memory scope, so a `float32` shared-buffer atomic on sm_90 is vectorized into a `CodeGenCUDA` overload whose relaxed branch is the global-address-space-only `atomicAdd(float2*/float4*)` builtin, which faults at launch on a shared pointer. This is a cross-pass interaction between two passes that each make a locally-defensible decision. `VectorizeLoop` rewrites the `float32` shared-buffer atomic on sm_90 to the `atomic_addx2`/`atomic_addx4` intrinsic. `CodeGenCUDA` then lowers that intrinsic to the sm≥90 `float32` `AtomicAddx2`/`AtomicAddx4` template overloads, whose relaxed branch is the CUDA `atomicAdd(float2*/float4*)` builtin — a global-address-space-only operation. Neither pass owns the "shared destinations cannot use the vector builtin" constraint, so nothing rejects or de-vectorizes the shared case, and the emitted code faults at launch.

<details><summary>Mechanism and source (the two passes)</summary>

- **Pass 1 — `VectorizeLoop` (`src/transform/vectorize_loop.cc`), scope-blind width choice.** The atomic-add SIMT loop is vectorized (enabled by [`LowerSIMT` → `LowerParallelLoop(..., should_vectorize=true)`, `src/cuda/op/atomic_add.cc:250-254`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/cuda/op/atomic_add.cc#L250-L254)), and the width is chosen by [`GetMaxAtomicVectorSize`, `vectorize_loop.cc:173-181`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/transform/vectorize_loop.cc#L173-L181) — `4` for `float32` when `TargetHasSMVersionGE(target, 90)`, `2` for fp16/bf16, `1` otherwise. The width then selects the intrinsic via [`GetVectorizedAtomicOp` at `vectorize_loop.cc:657-664`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/transform/vectorize_loop.cc#L657-L664). Neither function reads `dst`'s storage scope.
- **Pass 2 — `CodeGenCUDA` (`src/cuda/codegen/codegen_cuda.cc`), emits the global-only overload.** The `atomic_addx2`/`atomic_addx4` intrinsic is printed as `AtomicAddx2`/`AtomicAddx4` at [`codegen_cuda.cc:4847-4859`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/cuda/codegen/codegen_cuda.cc#L4847-L4859). For `float32` on sm≥90 these resolve to [`AtomicAddx2(float*)`, `atomic.h:772-783`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/tl_templates/cuda/atomic.h#L772-L783) whose relaxed branch is `atomicAdd(reinterpret_cast<float2*>(ref), add_val)` (line 776), and the width-4 sibling [`AtomicAddx4`, `atomic.h:802-812`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/tl_templates/cuda/atomic.h#L802-L812) whose relaxed branch is `atomicAdd(reinterpret_cast<float4*>(ref), add_val)`. Those `float2`/`float4` builtins operate only in the global address space; the header comment even states "Vectorized atomic operations only support global space" (line 810).
- Contrast the fp16 helper, which tolerates shared: [`AtomicAddx2(half_t*)`, `atomic.h:561-575`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/tl_templates/cuda/atomic.h#L561-L575) — relaxed branch is `atomicAdd(reinterpret_cast<half2*>(ref), ...)`, which accepts a shared pointer (confirmed on L40S). Below sm_90 the `float32` overloads take a `#else` scalar branch at [`atomic.h:836-869`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/tl_templates/cuda/atomic.h#L836-L869), but `GetMaxAtomicVectorSize` already returns 1 there, so that scalar overload is never even reached for fp32 on sm<90.

</details>

**Suggested fix.** The clean fix is in Pass 1: make `GetMaxAtomicVectorSize` (or the caller at `vectorize_loop.cc:657-664`) return width 1 for a `float32` atomic whose destination is a shared buffer, so it lowers to the scalar `AtomicAdd` (correct there). Alternatively, in Pass 2, route a shared pointer in the `float32` `AtomicAddx2`/`AtomicAddx4` overloads through the per-element fallback `AtomicAddx2Scalar`/`AtomicAddx4Scalar` (already present at [`atomic.h:285-296`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/tl_templates/cuda/atomic.h#L285-L296)) — but the device-side overload cannot see the compiler's scope information, so the Pass-1 fix is preferable. The bug itself is runtime-confirmed on sm_90 (H100, this session); the fix direction is unverified as a patch (not built/tested).

**Provenance.** The vectorized atomic-add feature was introduced in [#1676](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/1676) "Atomic Reduction Operations and Vectorization Enhancement". At v0.1.13 the width is chosen by `GetMaxAtomicVectorSize` in `src/transform/vectorize_loop.cc`, which reads dtype and SM version but not the destination scope; no scope check exists in that path. Not a regression: the `float32` vector overloads have been global-only since the feature shipped. The crash is reproduced at runtime on 0.1.13 (H100) this session. (The PR history above is from the tracker, not re-queried this session — no network.)

**Dedup.** I searched the open and closed tracker and found no existing report of the shared-scope face. The nearby atomic-add reports concern different mechanisms: #2688 (vectorized atomic drops `memory_order`), #2478 / #2561 (fp16/bf16 and integer `AtomicAddx4` dtype/width reinterpret), #2550 (sliced-destination crash); #1998 is a feature request that establishes shared relaxed atomics are supported through the generic builtins. (Tracker cross-references not re-queried online this session — verify before filing.)

**Reach.** This is a cross-pass interaction, not a single-site defect, and I want to be precise about what was and was not confirmed. The two passes are `VectorizeLoop` (`src/transform/vectorize_loop.cc`, picks the atomic width scope-blind) and `CodeGenCUDA` (`src/cuda/codegen/codegen_cuda.cc`, lowers the vectorized intrinsic to the global-only `float32` overload in `atomic.h`). The trigger needs three ingredients: (1) a `float32` atomic add into a **shared** destination, (2) written as a `T.Parallel` loop that maps ≥2 elements per thread (the auto-vectorized form, not explicit `T.get_thread_binding`), (3) run on sm_90 — the `GetMaxAtomicVectorSize` gate returns width>1 for `float32` only at sm≥90. The sm_90 float32-into-shared launch failure was run in the original session on an H100: the repro emits the width-2 `AtomicAddx2` on the shared `Bs` and aborts at launch (`InternalError`, CUDA launch failure). The only inferred (not-run) cell is the sm_90 float32-GLOBAL-destination row, which follows from the same width gate but with a legal global pointer.

**Two-level root and generalization (swept + run on L40S/sm_89, 0.1.13, this session).**

- **SOURCE-level root:** `GetMaxAtomicVectorSize` (`vectorize_loop.cc:173-181`) picks the atomic-add vector width from **dtype + SM version only, never the destination storage scope**; `GetVectorizedAtomicOp` (`vectorize_loop.cc:159-167`) then maps width→intrinsic. The fragile fact is confirmed at source: the only atomic op that reaches this vectorizer is `atomic_add` (`MutateAtomicAddExpr_` asserts `atomic_add_elem_op()` at `vectorize_loop.cc:630`). The crash surfaces only because the fp32 Pass-2 overload (`atomic.h:772-812`) resolves its relaxed branch to `atomicAdd(float2*/float4*)`, a global-address-space-only builtin.
- **OPERATOR-level root:** any op that (a) routes through `GetVectorizedAtomicOp` and (b) whose vectorized codegen overload requires the global address space. Today that set is exactly `{atomic_add}` × `{fp32 on sm≥90}`.

Axes swept (each cell RUN; scalar/vector decision read from emitted CUDA; values on sm_89 L40S — the fp32-shared **crash** itself is sm_90-only and was run earlier on H100, not re-runnable here):

| axis | cell tested (0.1.13) | emitted / observed | same-root? |
|---|---|---|---|
| main repro | fp32 shared, threads=128, 2/thread (sm_89) | scalar `AtomicAdd`, maxerr 0.0 | same root, **gated off** below sm_90 (width=1) |
| related-type | fp16 shared, 2/thread | `AtomicAddx2((&Bs..),*(uint1*)..)`, maxerr 0.0 | same Pass-1 scope-blind width; **distinct outcome** (fp16 overload accepts shared) |
| related-type | bfloat16 shared, 2/thread | `AtomicAddx2((&Bs..),*(uint1*)..)`, maxerr 0.0 | same Pass-1 root; distinct outcome (bf16 overload accepts shared) |
| similar-logic | fp16 vectorized atomic into **global**, 2/thread | `AtomicAddx2((&B..),*(uint1*)..)`, maxerr 0.0 | isolates scope: Pass-1 vectorizes regardless of scope; fp16 Pass-2 works in **both** scopes |
| related-operator | `atomic_max` fp16 shared, 2/thread | scalar `AtomicMax` (NOT `AtomicMaxx2`), maxerr 0.0 | **distinct, not filed** — max/min never vectorize (only `atomic_add` at `vectorize_loop.cc:630`), so they cannot reach the global-only vector overload |
| related-operator | `atomic_min` fp16 shared, 2/thread | scalar `AtomicMin` (NOT vectorized) | **distinct, not filed** — same reason (immune) |
| related-source | the atomic vectorizer path itself (`GetMaxAtomicVectorSize`/`GetVectorizedAtomicOp`) | source-confirmed: sole atomic vectorizer, `atomic_add`-only | same root; no sibling atomic op shares the fragile path |

Net: the scope-blind width choice in Pass 1 is **shared across fp16/bf16/fp32**, but the launch failure is confined to `float32`-into-shared-on-sm_90 because only the fp32 Pass-2 overload is global-only. fp16/bf16 exercise the identical Pass-1 root and run clean (their Pass-2 overload accepts shared). `atomic_max`/`atomic_min` are immune (never vectorized) — distinct, not filed. Boundary is narrow but real; kept specific to fp32×shared×sm_90 with the root named at the class level.

**Shipped-example run (PART 1, this session, L40S/sm_89 — verifies the "dodge" claims).** Both cited examples were located in the v0.1.13 tree and RUN verbatim:
- `examples/gemv/example_gemv.py` — `main(do_bench=False)` (N=K=256): **"Test passed!"**, no crash. It does a `float32` (`accum_dtype = T.float`) `atomic_add(C_shared[tn], ...)` into a **shared** buffer, but via explicit `T.get_thread_binding(0)` (scalar per thread, no `T.Parallel` vectorization) — dodges the bug exactly as the draft claims. (Also would not vectorize on sm_89 anyway.)
- `examples/deepseek_v32/topk_selector.py` — `test_topk_selector(batch=4, seq_len=4096, topk=128)`: ran clean, `selected/all = 1.0` for all rows. All its `atomic_add`s target `int32` shared histograms (`s_histogram`, `s_num_input` — integer → width 1), dodging the fp32 vector path as the draft claims.
Both example claims are CONFIRMED: the shipped code exercises float32/int shared atomics but avoids the ≥2-per-thread `T.Parallel` fp32 form, so CI stays green.

**Impact.** The trigger is narrow: `float32` atomic-add into a shared destination, written as a `T.Parallel` loop mapping ≥2 elements per thread, on sm_90. When it fires it aborts at launch with `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` — a loud, deterministic crash that blocks that kernel from running rather than silently corrupting any output, so it cannot slip into a workload and produce wrong results. Fixing it closes this scope×vectorization boundary class so the `float32` shared-atomic form lowers correctly like its scalar and fp16 siblings already do.

title: [BUG][Fuzzer][accepts-invalid] Region ops (`T.fill`/`T.clear`/`T.copy`) accept a sliced region whose `min+extent` exceeds the buffer, silently emitting an out-of-bounds write
body:
### Required prerequisites

- [x] I have read the documentation <https://tilelang.com>.
- [x] I have searched the Issue Tracker that this hasn't already been reported.

### What version of TileLang are you using?

0.1.13 (reproduced on 0.1.13; source cited at the `v0.1.13` tag).

### System information

NVIDIA L40S (`sm_89`), CUDA 12.8, Python 3.13, tilelang 0.1.13. The defect is in the target-independent `Fill` op constructor bound check, so it is not specific to one GPU.

### Problem description

A sliced `T.fill` whose start offset plus length runs past the destination buffer — e.g. `T.fill(As[6:12], 7)` into a shape-`8` buffer — is silently accepted and lowered to an out-of-bounds store, even though the op's own contract says such input must be rejected. The `Fill` constructor's static bound check validates `min >= 0` and `extent <= shape` per dimension, but never checks `min + extent <= shape`, so a slice with a nonzero start slips through: `min = 6 >= 0` ✓ and `extent = 6 <= 8` ✓ both pass, while `min + extent = 12 > 8` is out of bounds.

The generated CUDA writes 4 elements past the end of the shared buffer:

<details><summary>Generated store (this session)</summary>

```cpp
// As is alloc_shared((8,), int32); the fill emits, for threadIdx.x in [0,6):
As[(((int)threadIdx.x) + 6)] = 7;      // writes indices 6..11 -> 8,9,10,11 are OOB
```

</details>

The nearest sibling — a pure-extent overflow `T.fill(As[0:12], 7)` (extent `12 > 8`) — **is** cleanly rejected by the very same check (`region[0] = 12 > 8`), which shows the guard exists and is meant to cover this; the min-offset case escapes it only because the start term is omitted.

### Reproducible example code

```python
import tilelang, tilelang.language as T

NBUF = 8

@T.prim_func
def main(B: T.Tensor((NBUF,), "int32")):
    with T.Kernel(1, threads=32):
        As = T.alloc_shared((NBUF,), "int32")
        T.fill(As[6:12], 7)        # min=6, extent=6 -> writes indices 6..11, 4 past shape 8
        T.copy(As, B)

tilelang.compile(main)             # SILENTLY ACCEPTED (compiles); emits As[tid+6]=7

# CONTROL A (rejected as it should be) — pure extent overflow, same buffer:
#   T.fill(As[0:12], 7)  ->  InternalError "region[0] = 12 > 8"
# CONTROL B (correctly accepted) — in-bounds slice:
#   T.fill(As[2:8], 7)   ->  compiles, fills exactly indices 2..7
```

### Traceback

```
No traceback — the kernel compiles and runs to completion; the fill silently
writes 4 elements (indices 8..11) past the end of the 8-element shared buffer.
```

### Expected behavior

An out-of-bounds fill region has no valid target — indices 8..11 are past the end of an 8-element buffer, so there is nothing legal to write there — and the op should reject it, exactly as its docstring promises ("checks that mins >= 0 and extents do not exceed the corresponding destination shape extents … will terminate (via ICHECK) if inputs are … out of bounds") and exactly as the pure-extent-overflow sibling already does. Instead it silently accepts and emits an out-of-bounds shared-memory store.

### Additional context

**Root cause.** The `Fill` operator's static bound check mis-analyzes a sliced fill region: it checks the start and the length independently (`min >= 0`, `extent <= shape`) but never their sum against the shape, so a slice whose start-plus-length exceeds the buffer is treated as in-bounds. The lowering then honors the nonzero start (`region[i]->min + var`) and emits the out-of-range store.

- The incomplete check: [`src/op/fill.cc#L111-L127`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/op/fill.cc#L111-L127) — `ICHECK_GE(min, 0)` and `ICHECK_LE(extent, shape)`, no `min + extent <= shape`.
- The min-offset store the missing check lets through: [`src/op/fill.cc#L164`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/op/fill.cc#L164) (`dst_indices.push_back(region[i]->min + var)`).
- The documented contract it violates: [`src/op/fill.cc#L78-L92`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/op/fill.cc#L78-L92).

**Suggested fix.** In the `Fill` constructor bound check (`src/op/fill.cc#L111-L127`), when both `region[i].min` and `region[i].extent` (and the shape) are statically known, add `ICHECK_LE(min + extent, shape)` alongside the existing checks, so a sliced fill past the end is rejected with the same actionable message the pure-extent case already produces.

**Same root, wider scope — the OOB-region check is per-op and inconsistent.** `Fill` is not the only region op that accepts an out-of-bounds sliced region; the bound check is implemented separately in each op rather than once at the slice/`BufferRegion` layer, so the ops disagree. Verified this session on 0.1.13 (dst slice `[6:12]` into a shape-8 buffer):

| op | check in source | OOB sliced region → | 
|---|---|---|
| `T.fill` | only `extent <= shape` (`fill.cc:122`, no `min` term) | accepted → emits `S[tid+6]=7` (writes 8..11) |
| `T.clear` | same `Fill` op (`fill_op.py:40`) | accepted (same path as fill) |
| `T.copy` | a `min + extent <= shape` expression exists but is **not** a bound guard (see below) | accepted → emits `Bs[tid+6]=Src[tid]`, runs and corrupts `B[7]` |

`fill`/`clear` lack the `min` term entirely. `copy` *appears* to have the right check — `min >= 0 && min + extent <= shape` at [`copy_analysis.cc:374`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/cuda/op/copy_analysis.cc#L374) — but that is `CanProveCopyInBounds`, whose only caller ([`copy_analysis.cc:656`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/cuda/op/copy_analysis.cc#L656)) uses it as an **optimization gate**: `layout_dependent_tma_available = has_layout_map && !is_cutedsl && CanProveCopyInBounds(...)`. When the region is *not* provably in bounds it returns false, which merely disables the TMA 1D fast path and falls back to the ordinary copy — it never rejects. So an OOB copy is not caught at all; it just takes the slow path and emits the out-of-bounds store. In other words no region op rejects an out-of-bounds sliced region — `fill`'s incomplete `extent <= shape` is the *only* actual reject check in the family, and even it misses the `min` term. Because there is no shared bound check, fixing `fill` alone leaves `copy`/`clear` writing out of bounds; a single bound check at the region-construction layer (where every op's slice is formed) would cover all of them. `T.fill` on a `fragment` is rejected here only incidentally — a layout check trips first, not a bound check.

**Provenance.** The `region.min + var` store offset and the extent-only bound check were both introduced by **#1189 (`a03df604`, "[Feature] Enhance fill operation to support various buffer types")** — #1189 added the nonzero-start slice support but wrote the guard as `extent <= shape` without the `min` term, so the sliced-fill OOB has never been caught (never-worked, not a regression). The file was later relocated (not re-introduced) by the `TileOperator`/backend refactors; the check is unchanged through `v0.1.13`. Reproduced at runtime on 0.1.13 this session: `T.fill(As[6:12],7)` into a shape-8 shared buffer silently compiles and emits `As[threadIdx.x + 6] = 7` (writes 8..11), while the pure-extent sibling `As[0:12]` is rejected (`extent 12 > shape 8`) and the in-bounds `As[2:8]` compiles.

**Dedup.** I searched the open and closed Issue Tracker and found no existing report of this bound-check defect; none names the omitted `min + extent` term in the sliced-fill bound check. It is distinct from #2942 (`T.fill` of a row-offset **fragment** sub-region silently fills the *wrong rows* — a non-injective layout-mapping miscompile, disposition compute-correctly), which is a different object (fragment vs shared), symptom (wrong data vs out-of-bounds write), and root (layout mapping vs the missing bound-check term). This one is the constructor bound check accepting an illegal out-of-bounds region.

**Reach.** Sliced `T.fill` (`T.fill(buf[a:b], v)`) is ordinary usage for initializing a sub-region of a tile. The trigger is any slice whose `start + length` exceeds the buffer — an easy off-by-one when a stride/offset is computed. No shipped example or test passes such a slice (they fill in-bounds), so CI stays green.

**Impact.** The trigger is narrow — it needs a statically-out-of-bounds *sliced* fill (nonzero start whose start+length exceeds the shape); a pure-extent overflow is already caught, and in-bounds slices are fine. But when it fires the consequence is severe: instead of a diagnostic it silently emits an out-of-bounds shared-memory store (a memory-safety / soundness gap), deterministic and past the buffer end, corrupting whatever aliases those slots — the kind of error the bound check exists to prevent.

title: [BUG][Fuzzer][ice-on-valid-code] Reading a `T.Pipelined` producer shared buffer after the loop crashes the compiler instead of compiling
body:
### Required prerequisites

- [x] I have read the documentation <https://tilelang.com>.
- [x] I have searched the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues) and no similar issue was found.

### What version of TileLang are you using?

0.1.13

### System information

TileLang 0.1.13 / PyTorch 2.8.0 / CUDA 12.8; NVIDIA L40S (sm_89). The crash is in a target-independent host pass (`LayoutInference`), so it is not hardware-specific.

### Problem description

A shared buffer that is written inside a `T.Pipelined(..., num_stages>=2)` loop and then read *after* the loop crashes compilation with an internal assert, while the identical kernel with `num_stages=1` compiles and runs:

```
InternalError: Check failed: (az->CanProveEqual(input_shape_product * rescale_num, shape_product * rescale_den)) is false:
InputShape() = (3, 64, 32) shape = (64, 32), rescale_num = 16, rescale_den = 16
```

The `(3, 64, 32)` is the buffer after pipeline multi-versioning has prepended the `num_stages=3` version dimension; `(64, 32)` is the buffer's original shape as seen at the post-loop read. Same trigger with `num_stages=1` (no versioning) compiles and runs correctly, so the crash is specific to the multi-versioning path — not the read itself. Not a regression — see Provenance.

### Reproducible example code

```python
import tilelang
import tilelang.language as T
import torch

M, K, BK = 64, 128, 32

def build(num_stages):
    @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[1])
    def kern():
        @T.prim_func
        def main(A: T.Tensor((M, K), "float16"), Out: T.Tensor((M, BK), "float16")):
            with T.Kernel(1, threads=128) as bx:
                As = T.alloc_shared((M, BK), "float16")   # producer, written each stage
                Bs = T.alloc_shared((BK, M), "float16")
                Cf = T.alloc_fragment((M, M), "float32")
                T.clear(Cf)
                for k in T.Pipelined(K // BK, num_stages=num_stages):
                    T.copy(A[0:M, k * BK:(k + 1) * BK], As)
                    for i, j in T.Parallel(BK, M):
                        Bs[i, j] = T.float16(1.0)
                    T.gemm(As, Bs, Cf)
                T.copy(As, Out)                            # read As AFTER the pipelined loop
        return main
    return kern()

# CONTROL: same kernel, same post-loop read, num_stages=1 (no multi-versioning) -> compiles + runs
f = build(num_stages=1)
a = torch.randn(M, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
o = f(a)
print("num_stages=1 :", "COMPILED+RAN, out", tuple(o.shape))   # -> COMPILED+RAN, out (64, 32)

# TRIGGER: num_stages>=2 multi-versions As; the post-loop read then crashes the compiler
f = build(num_stages=3)                                        # -> InternalError (see Traceback)
print("num_stages=3 : COMPILED (unexpected)")
```

### Traceback

```
  File "tilelang/cuda/pipeline.py", line 117, in CUDAPassPipelineBodyPrologue
    mod = tilelang.transform.LayoutInference()(mod)
  ...
  in tvm::tl::LayoutInferencer::Substitute(tvm::tirx::PrimFunc)
  in tvm::tl::BufferUseDefCollector::Run()
  in tvm::tl::BufferUseDefCollector::RunInferStep(...)
  in tvm::tl::BufferUseDefCollector::RunInferStep(...)::{lambda(Buffer, Layout)#1}::operator()(...)
  File "/project/src/layout/layout.cc", line 871, in tvm::tl::LayoutNode::Reshape(...)
tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (az->CanProveEqual(input_shape_product * rescale_num, shape_product * rescale_den)) is false: InputShape() = (3, 64, 32) shape = (64, 32), rescale_num = 16, rescale_den = 16
```

### Expected behavior

Compilation completes instead of tripping an internal assert. The two consistent outcomes both seem reasonable: either the post-loop read is honored (reading the buffer's last-written version), or, if reading a pipeline-versioned producer after the loop is not intended to be supported, a clean diagnostic at the frontend that names the buffer and the pattern. An internal `CanProveEqual` assert deep in layout inference is neither.

### Additional context

**Root cause.** Two passes disagree about a shared buffer that is both a `T.gemm` operand *and* read after the pipelined loop. The multi-version buffer rewriter (run by the software-pipeline stack) rewrites the buffer's allocation to carry a leading `num_stages` version dimension, so its declared shape becomes `[3, 64, 32]`. `LayoutInference` independently infers an MMA-operand layout for that buffer over its original `[64, 32]` shape (from the `T.gemm` use), then — because the versioned allocation and the operand use are the same underlying storage — propagates the `[64, 32]` layout onto the `[3, 64, 32]` alias via `LayoutNode::Reshape`. That reshape assumes the two shapes differ only by element width (an alias-reinterpret rescale) and fails the storage-product invariant: `prod([3,64,32])*16 != prod([64,32])*16`. The trigger is narrow and specific: adjacent-cell probes (see Reach) show it needs the read-after buffer to carry an inferred MMA-operand layout — a versioned shared buffer that is *not* a gemm operand, or the gemm accumulator fragment, is read after the loop without crashing.

<details><summary>Where it happens (0.1.13)</summary>

- The version dimension is prepended in [`RewriteAllocBuffer`, `multi_version_buffer_rewriter.cc:494`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/cuda/transform/multi_version_buffer_rewriter.cc#L494) — [`shape.insert(begin, num_versions)`, :503](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/cuda/transform/multi_version_buffer_rewriter.cc#L503) → `[64,32]` becomes `[3,64,32]`.
- The rewriter's own [BufferLoad guard, `:769`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/cuda/transform/multi_version_buffer_rewriter.cc#L769) (`ICHECK(version_index.defined()) << "Versioned buffer load escaped pipeline stage context"`) shows the escaped-use case was anticipated, but a post-loop read reaching layout inference is not caught there.
- The crash surfaces in the alias-propagation path of layout inference, which reshapes the inferred layout onto a same-data sibling assuming the two shapes differ only by element width: [`layout_inference.cc:184`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/transform/layout_inference.cc#L184).
- The assert is the storage-product check in [`LayoutNode::Reshape`, `layout.cc:871`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/layout/layout.cc#L871): `prod([3,64,32])*16 != prod([64,32])*16`.

</details>

**Suggested fix.** The multi-version rewriter should detect a use of a versioned buffer outside the pipeline stage context (the case its `:769` guard already describes) and either keep that use on an un-versioned view or reject it at the frontend with a clear message; alternatively the layout-inference alias propagation at `:184` should account for a prepended version dimension rather than treating the shape difference as an element-width rescale. This touches either the pipeline rewriter or layout inference, so it is not a one-line change (not verified end-to-end).

**Provenance.** The version-dimension prepend is part of the multi-version buffer rewriter, present since it shipped (`multi_version_buffer_rewriter.cc`, created in [#2166](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/2166), merged 2026-05-12; software-pipeline transforms later refactored in [#2245](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/2245)). The equivalent versioning existed inline in the pipeline pass before that split. The crash is the interaction of this versioning with layout-inference alias propagation; I did not pin a single introducing PR for the interaction.

**Dedup.** I searched the open and closed tracker and found no existing report of this exact crash. The closest relative is [#2309](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues/2309) (open, "LayoutInference crash for sibling `T.Pipelined` loops sharing `alloc_shared` buffers with different `num_stages`") — a **distinct bug that shares this one's underlying theme**: both are a `T.Pipelined` × shared-buffer interaction where the buffer's *actual multi-versioned storage layout* disagrees with the shape a later use assumes, and `LayoutInference` cannot reconcile the two. They differ in the triggering structure: #2309 needs **two sibling pipelined loops** that request **different `num_stages`** for the *same* `alloc_shared` (the conflict is between the two loops' version counts), whereas this bug needs a **single** pipelined loop whose versioned MMA-operand buffer is **read after the loop** (the conflict is between the versioned allocation `[num_stages,…]` and the operand's original `[…]` shape at the post-loop read). Same family — the multi-version rewriter's prepended version dimension not being accounted for downstream — but a different trigger and a different reconciliation site, so they warrant separate reports (and likely a shared fix in how versioned aliases carry their layout). Two further, more distant relatives: [#2528](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues/2528) also involves the multi-version rewriter but is a distinct defect — a runtime `CUDA error: misaligned address` from missing 128B padding on a 1-D TMA copy, not a compile-time layout-inference assert; and [#2609](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues/2609) is also a `LayoutNode::Reshape` failure but for a cross-element-width swizzled `T.view`, with no pipeline versioning involved.

**Impact.** The trigger is narrow: a shared `T.gemm`-operand buffer read after a `num_stages>=2` pipelined loop, a pattern the shipped examples happen to dodge by reading the fragment accumulator instead. `examples/gemm/example_gemm.py` was **run verbatim on 0.1.13** and compiles+runs+passes (`All check passed.`, latency 0.033 ms): it uses `num_stages=3` but copies the fragment accumulator `C_local` — not a shared operand — after the loop, so it never hits the versioned-alias reshape. When the bug fires the failure is a compile-time internal assert in `LayoutInference` — loud and deterministic, caught the moment the kernel is built; it corrupts no data and cannot reach a running workload silently. Fixing it either lets a legal "fill a shared operand tile across the loop, reuse its final contents after" kernel compile or replaces the deep `CanProveEqual` assert with a clear frontend diagnostic naming the buffer and pattern.

**Reach.** The root is a two-pass interaction — the **multi-version buffer rewriter** (`src/cuda/transform/multi_version_buffer_rewriter.cc`, driven by the software-pipeline stack) prepends the version dimension, and **`LayoutInference`** (`src/transform/layout_inference.cc`, run from `tilelang/cuda/pipeline.py:117`) reshapes an MMA-operand layout onto that versioned alias. Neither pass is wrong in isolation; the assert fires only where they compose. I ran six isolated cells on 0.1.13 (fresh cache each, one kernel per process) to map the boundary:

- `num_stages=1` (control) — **COMPILED+RAN**, `out (64,32)`. No versioning, no crash.
- `num_stages=2`, gemm-operand `As` read after loop — **CRASH**, `InputShape() = (2,64,32)`. Same assert, version dim = `num_stages`. **Same root** as the `num_stages=3` trigger.
- `num_stages=3`, gemm-operand `As` read after loop — **CRASH**, `InputShape() = (3,64,32)`. The headline trigger.
- `num_stages=3`, read the *fragment accumulator* after loop (the canonical GEMM pattern, `examples/gemm/example_gemm.py` copies `C_local` not the shared operand) — **COMPILED+RAN**, `out (64,64)`. **Distinct path**: fragment read-after does not hit the versioned-alias reshape. This is why shipped examples and CI stay green.
- `num_stages=3`, read-after buffer written in-loop but **not** a gemm operand (gemm uses a separate shared pair) — **COMPILED+RAN**, `out (64,32)`. **Distinct**: without an inferred MMA-operand layout there is nothing to reshape onto the versioned alias.
- `num_stages=3`, gemm-operand `As` written by `T.Parallel` instead of `T.copy`, read after loop — **CRASH**, `InputShape() = (3,64,32)`. **Same root**: the discriminator is *being an MMA operand read after the loop*, not how the buffer is written.

So the necessary ingredients are all three of: `num_stages>=2` (versioning), the read-after buffer is a `T.gemm` operand (so `LayoutInference` gives it an MMA layout), and it is read after the loop (so the versioned allocation and the operand use alias the same storage). `T.Pipelined` with `num_stages>=2` is itself ubiquitous (grep at this SHA: **130** example files use `T.Pipelined`, **1105** `num_stages` sites under `examples/`); the rarer combination is reusing an MMA-operand shared tile after the pipelined loop, which nothing in the `T.Pipelined` docstring disclaims.

**Generalization (root + 4-axis sweep, all cells run on 0.1.13).** *Two-level root.*
- **SOURCE-level root.** The fragile code is the alias-reinterpret branch of layout inference: [`layout_inference.cc:184`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/transform/layout_inference.cc#L184) calls `LayoutNode::Reshape(sib->shape, ..., old_bits, new_bits)` for any two buffers sharing storage, assuming they differ only by element **width**. When one alias is the pipeline-versioned allocation (`[num_stages, ...]`) the shape differs by a prepended *count* dimension, not a width, and the storage-product ICHECK at [`layout.cc:871`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/8001cc4ccf6149382d2019654a19f59c1d4d0482/src/layout/layout.cc#L871) fails. The version dimension itself is prepended upstream by `RewriteAllocBuffer` in the multi-version buffer rewriter (`multi_version_buffer_rewriter.cc:494/503`). Neither pass is wrong alone; the assert fires only where they compose.
- **OPERATOR-level root.** Being an **MMA operand read after the pipelined loop.** The `T.gemm` use gives the shared buffer an MMA-operand layout that must be reshaped onto the versioned alias; the *read* is what makes the versioned allocation and the operand use the same storage. Related ops correlate only if they too impose a layout on a versioned shared buffer that is then read post-loop.

**4-axis sweep** (each cell run in a fresh `/tmp/gen_23_*` dir, fresh cache, one kernel/process):

| axis | cell tested | result | same-root? |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | `num_stages=1`, LHS operand read-after (control) | COMPILED+RAN, out (64,32) | n/a (no versioning) |
| baseline | `num_stages=2/3`, LHS operand `As` read-after | CRASH `InputShape()=(2,64,32)` / `(3,64,32)`, rescale 16/16 | headline |
| similar-logic | operand read-after via `T.Parallel` elementwise (not `T.copy`) | CRASH `(3,64,32)`, rescale 16 | **same-root** — read *op* is irrelevant |
| similar-logic | operand written by `T.Parallel` instead of `T.copy`, read-after | CRASH `(3,64,32)` | **same-root** — write *op* is irrelevant |
| related-source | fragment accumulator read-after (the `example_gemm.py` path) | COMPILED+RAN, out (64,64) | distinct — fragment has no versioned-alias reshape |
| related-source | versioned shared buffer read-after that is **not** a gemm operand | COMPILED+RAN, out (64,32) | distinct — no MMA layout to reshape |
| related-operator | read the **RHS** gemm operand `Bs` after loop (vs LHS) | COMPILED+RAN, out (32,64) | distinct — RHS operand layout reshapes cleanly onto the versioned alias; only LHS crashes |
| related-type | **bf16** LHS operand read-after | CRASH `(3,64,32)`, rescale 16/16 | **same-root** — dtype-independent within 16-bit |
| related-type | **fp8 (e4m3)** LHS operand read-after | CRASH `(3,64,32)`, rescale **8/8** | **same-root** — width-independent; storage-bits change but the product mismatch (prepended count dim) is unchanged |

**Findings.** The root is dtype/width-independent (fp16, bf16, fp8 all crash identically; the `rescale` numbers track element-storage-bits but the failure is the prepended count dimension, not any width mismatch) and read-op/write-op-independent (`T.copy` and `T.Parallel` both crash). The discriminator is exactly *being an LHS MMA operand read after the loop*: fragment-accumulator reads, non-operand shared reads, and **RHS-operand** reads all compile. The RHS-vs-LHS asymmetry (draft's previously-unpinned note) is now confirmed by direct test — only the LHS operand crashes; the RHS operand's inferred layout reshapes onto the versioned alias without tripping the product check. This is a **narrow, specific** boundary, not a class, so the title and Problem are **kept specific**. No new distinct-adjacent bug and no separately-fileable neighbor were found: every crashing neighbor is the same root, every non-crashing neighbor is a genuinely distinct (correct) path.

**Example-run result (PART 1).** `examples/gemm/example_gemm.py` (v0.1.13) run verbatim: **COMPILED+RAN, `All check passed.`**, latency 0.033 ms. It uses `num_stages=3` but copies the fragment accumulator `C_local` after the loop (source confirmed) — so the shipped example does **not** exercise this bug; it dodges it exactly as the Reach section claims. This is honest evidence that the pattern is off the CI path, which is why the crash went unreported, not evidence that the trigger is common.

title: [BUG] Resolve symlinked nvcc before deriving CUDA_HOME
body:
### Prerequisite

- [x] I have searched existing issues and related NVRTC include discovery work.

### Problem

When nvcc is exposed through a symlink, _find_cuda_home() derives CUDA_HOME from the symlink's directory instead of the compiler's real location. This commonly occurs with NVIDIA's pip CUDA packages.

On this system:

| Path | Result |
| --- | --- |
| /home/morluto/.local/bin/nvcc | symlink |
| resolved compiler | .../site-packages/nvidia/cu13/bin/nvcc |
| previous discovered CUDA_HOME | /home/morluto/.local |
| expected CUDA_HOME | .../site-packages/nvidia/cu13 |

The incorrect root omits include/cuda_runtime.h, causing TileLang CUDA compilation to fail even though a working NVCC installation is available.

### Reproduction

1. Put a symlink to a standard <CUDA_HOME>/bin/nvcc on PATH.
2. Leave CUDA_HOME and CUDA_PATH unset.
3. Call tilelang.env._find_cuda_home().

The result is the parent of the symlink location rather than the CUDA installation root.

### Expected behavior

Auto-discovery should resolve nvcc before deriving its CUDA root. Explicit CUDA_HOME and CUDA_PATH should retain precedence.

### Proposed fix

Resolve the shutil.which("nvcc") result with os.path.realpath() before applying the existing parent-directory logic, with a deterministic symlink regression test.

title: [BUG][Fuzzer][wrong-code] Hopper `T.gemm_sp` emits code that omits the ISA-required `fence.proxy.async` before the sparse WGMMA — silently reads stale operand data
body:
### Required prerequisites - [x] I have read the documentation . - [x] I have searched the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues) that this hasn't already been reported. (comment there if it has.) ### What version of TileLang are you using? 0.1.11 (source at `cd37ed5fc35ae7a60a1277c8eb49028174ac51e6`). Also live on `main` (`1e075149`). ### System information NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (sm_90), CUDA 13.0, tilelang 0.1.11. `fence.proxy.async` is a Hopper construct (`InjectFenceProxy` is gated on `TargetHasBulkCopy`, i.e. sm_90+), so the defect is sm_90-specific. Blackwell (sm_100) is affected by inspection — the blockscaled sparse builtin `ptx_tcgen05_mma_blockscaled_ss` has the same omission — but I did not run it. ### Problem description **`T.gemm_sp` emits code that omits the `fence.proxy.async` the PTX proxy model requires** between a generic-proxy write to a shared WGMMA operand tile and the async-proxy `wgmma.mma_async.sp` read of that same tile. On the identical kernel, the dense `T.gemm` emits the fence and the sparse `T.gemm_sp` emits **zero**. Per PTX ISA §9.7.16.7.1 — *"An async proxy fence must be used to establish an ordering between prior writes to shared memory matrices and subsequent reads of the same matrices in a `wgmma.mma_async` instruction"* — the generated sparse code is **incorrect by the documented contract**: the WGMMA is permitted to read stale/torn operand data, a silent wrong result, with nothing ordering the two. This is a wrong-code defect in the emitted PTX/SASS, established at the code level (counts + adjacency below) and grounded in the ISA. I did not force a divergent value out of `T.gemm_sp` itself on the tested H100 — an incidental `bar.sync` (the pipeline `__syncthreads()`) happens to drain the write on that schedule — but that barrier is **not** the ISA-required ordering (§8.7: it is a different proxy, so it establishes no happens-before edge), and a minimal control carrying the exact "`bar.sync` present, proxy fence absent" fingerprint **does** race the silicon (see Additional context). The two kernels below are identical except `T.gemm` vs `T.gemm_sp`; both put a `B_s[i,j] += 3` generic store right before the matmul. `T.gemm` emits one `fence.proxy.async`; `T.gemm_sp` emits zero.
Emitted PTX and SASS — the required fence is present for dense, absent for sparse (H100, sm_90, CUDA 13.0) Counts (grep of the emitted code): CUDA `fence_proxy_async` dense **1** / sparse **0**; PTX `fence.proxy.async` dense **1** / sparse **0**; SASS main-loop proxy fence (`MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` + `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` right after the generic operand store) dense **present** / sparse **absent** (both kernels share one *prologue* `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`; the load-bearing difference is the main-loop one). ``` === PTX, dense (proxy fence PRESENT) === wgmma.fence.sync.aligned; // register/accumulator fence — NOT the proxy fence fence.proxy.async.shared::cta; // <-- the generic->async-proxy fence wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64n128k16.f32.f16.f16 {...}; === PTX, sparse (proxy fence ABSENT) === wgmma.fence.sync.aligned; // register fence only wgmma.mma_async.sp.sync.aligned.m64n128k32.f32.f16.f16 {...}; // async read, unfenced // the generic operand store st.shared.v4.u32 precedes this with nothing ordering it === SASS, dense: STS.128 -> MEMBAR.ALL.CTA ; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S ; WARPGROUP.ARRIVE ; HGMMA.64x128x16.F32 === SASS, sparse: STS.128 -> BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING ; WARPGROUP.ARRIVE ; HGMMA.SP.64x128x32.F32 (full scan of the sparse store->WGMMA.SP window: zero MEMBAR / FENCE.VIEW / DEPBAR) ``` The `wgmma.fence.sync.aligned` present in **both** is the accumulator/register fence, not the generic→async-proxy fence — only dense additionally emits `fence.proxy.async`. In SASS, where dense has `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`, sparse has only a `BAR.SYNC` — a barrier, which the PTX memory model (§8.7) does not accept as a substitute because it does not change an access's proxy.
### Reproducible example code ```python import tilelang, tilelang.language as T from tilelang.utils.sparse import get_e_factor M = N = K = 256; bM = bN = 128; bK = 64 e_dtype = "uint8"; e_factor = get_e_factor(T.float16, e_dtype) def dense(): # CONTROL: gets the fence @T.prim_func def main(A: T.Tensor((M, K), T.float16), B: T.Tensor((K, N), T.float16), C: T.Tensor((M, N), "float32")): with T.Kernel(T.ceildiv(N, bN), T.ceildiv(M, bM), threads=128) as (bx, by): A_s = T.alloc_shared((bM, bK), T.float16); B_s = T.alloc_shared((bK, bN), T.float16) C_l = T.alloc_fragment((bM, bN), "float32"); T.clear(C_l) for k in T.Pipelined(T.ceildiv(K, bK), num_stages=2): T.copy(A[by * bM, k * bK], A_s); T.copy(B[k * bK, bx * bN], B_s) for i, j in T.Parallel(bK, bN): B_s[i, j] = B_s[i, j] + T.float16(3) # generic-proxy write to operand tile T.gemm(A_s, B_s, C_l) T.copy(C_l, C[by * bM, bx * bN]) return main def sparse(): # BUG: no fence @T.prim_func def main(A_sp: T.Tensor((M, K // 2), T.float16), E: T.Tensor((M, K // e_factor), e_dtype), B: T.Tensor((K, N), T.float16), C: T.Tensor((M, N), "float32")): with T.Kernel(T.ceildiv(N, bN), T.ceildiv(M, bM), threads=128) as (bx, by): A_s = T.alloc_shared((bM, bK // 2), T.float16); E_s = T.alloc_shared((bM, bK // e_factor), e_dtype) B_s = T.alloc_shared((bK, bN), T.float16); C_l = T.alloc_fragment((bM, bN), "float32"); T.clear(C_l) for k in T.Pipelined(T.ceildiv(K, bK), num_stages=2): T.copy(A_sp[by * bM, k * bK // 2], A_s); T.copy(E[by * bM, k * bK // e_factor], E_s) T.copy(B[k * bK, bx * bN], B_s) for i, j in T.Parallel(bK, bN): B_s[i, j] = B_s[i, j] + T.float16(3) # same generic write T.gemm_sp(A_s, E_s, B_s, C_l, transpose_A=False, transpose_E=False, transpose_B=False) T.copy(C_l, C[by * bM, bx * bN]) return main for name, fn, idx in [("DENSE T.gemm", dense, 2), ("SPARSE T.gemm_sp", sparse, 3)]: k = tilelang.compile(fn(), out_idx=[idx]) print(f"{name}: fence.proxy.async count = {k.get_kernel_source().count('fence_proxy_async')}") # DENSE T.gemm: fence.proxy.async count = 1 # SPARSE T.gemm_sp: fence.proxy.async count = 0 <-- missing ``` ### Traceback No traceback — both kernels compile and run to completion. The defect is missing memory-ordering in the emitted code: the generated sparse PTX/SASS omits the `fence.proxy.async` the ISA requires, so the sparse WGMMA is permitted to read a stale/torn operand — a silent wrong result whenever the (absent) ordering actually matters. ### Expected behavior `T.gemm_sp` should emit the same `fence.proxy.async` that `T.gemm` emits when a generic-proxy shared write precedes it — i.e. the sparse WGMMA should be treated as an async-proxy op by `InjectFenceProxy`, exactly like the dense WGMMA already is. cutlass emits this fence for the same generic→async-proxy transition: [`cutlass/arch/barrier.h#L715-L721`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/b2dd65dc864e09688245b316ac46c4a6cd07e15c/include/cutlass/arch/barrier.h#L715-L721) (`fence_view_async_shared()` = `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta`) and [`cute/arch/copy_sm90_tma.hpp#L1214-L1217`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/b2dd65dc864e09688245b316ac46c4a6cd07e15c/include/cute/arch/copy_sm90_tma.hpp#L1214-L1217) (`tma_store_fence()`). The tilelang pass already encodes this rule for the dense path, so the sparse path being unfenced looks like an omission in the intrinsic list rather than an intentional difference. ### Additional context **Root cause.** `InjectFenceProxy` does not recognize the sparse WGMMA builtins as async-proxy operations, so it omits the `fence.proxy.async` before a generic write that precedes a sparse matmul.
Mechanism — the sparse variants are missing from the async-intrinsic list The pass classifies calls via `IsAsyncIntrinsic` ([`inject_fence_proxy.cc#L99-L106`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/cd37ed5fc35ae7a60a1277c8eb49028174ac51e6/src/cuda/transform/inject_fence_proxy.cc#L99-L106)). That list contains the dense WGMMA builtins `ptx_wgmma_ss`/`ptx_wgmma_rs` and the dense tcgen05 ops, but **omits the sparse variants** `ptx_wgmma_sp_ss`, `ptx_wgmma_sp_rs`, and `ptx_tcgen05_mma_blockscaled_ss` (all public builtins). `T.gemm`/`T.gemm_sp` are lowered by `LowerTileOp` ([`pipeline.py#L117`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/cd37ed5fc35ae7a60a1277c8eb49028174ac51e6/tilelang/cuda/pipeline.py#L117)) **before** `InjectFenceProxy` runs ([`pipeline.py#L229`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/cd37ed5fc35ae7a60a1277c8eb49028174ac51e6/tilelang/cuda/pipeline.py#L229)): dense lowers to `ptx_wgmma_ss` (in the list → fenced), sparse lowers to `ptx_wgmma_sp_ss` (not in the list → not fenced). The default for unlisted intrinsics is now fail-open (`return ProxyEvent::kNone`), so the sparse op slips through with no fence. `T.gemm_sp` is a public op exported into the `T` namespace.
**Suggested fix (one line).** Add `ptx_wgmma_sp_ss()`, `ptx_wgmma_sp_rs()`, and `ptx_tcgen05_mma_blockscaled_ss()` to the `IsAsyncIntrinsic` disjunction, alongside their dense siblings. All three C++ symbols already exist. After adding them, the sparse repro emits `fence.proxy.async count = 1`, matching the dense control — restoring the ISA-required ordering the emitted code was missing. **Wrong-code confirmed in the emitted code; runtime symptom masked on the tested silicon.** The defect is confirmed at the level a `[wrong-code]` classification requires — the generated PTX/SASS omits the `fence.proxy.async` that PTX ISA §9.7.16.7.1 says *must* order a generic write to a shared WGMMA operand ahead of the async `wgmma.mma_async.sp` read; dense emits it, sparse does not (counts + adjacency in Problem description). I did **not** force a divergent numerical result out of `T.gemm_sp` itself (~29,000 iterations matched a manual-`T.fence_proxy_async()` control bit-exact), because an incidental partial `bar.sync` (the pipeline `__syncthreads()`) drains the generic write on this schedule. That `bar.sync` is not the ISA-required ordering — per PTX §8.7, two operations are morally strong only if performed via the *same* proxy, so a generic-proxy barrier establishes no ordering against an async-proxy read — so it protects neither other Hopper silicon/schedules, nor other tile shapes, nor Blackwell, nor any refactor that moves or removes it. The code is wrong; the current schedule merely masks the symptom.
Positive control — the silicon does race when the drain is truly absent On a minimally-derived single-warpgroup WGMMA kernel, three variants differ only in the ordering primitive between the generic operand write and the async read: **A** = nothing, **B** = `fence.proxy.async` (correct golden), **C** = `bar.sync` only, fence removed (the exact `T.gemm_sp` fingerprint). Racing C against the fenced golden B on identical fp16 inputs under a concurrent spoiler kernel, on H100 sm_90: - 100k iterations, seed 0x1001: **2** divergences, worst |diff| **30.9**; - 1M iterations, seed 0xBEEF (different GPU): **30** divergences, worst |diff| **31.4**; a captured launch had 512/8192 output elements wrong (a torn/partial operand read); - fence-vs-fence control (B vs B, same input): **0** divergences — the golden is deterministic, so every C divergence is a genuine ordering effect. This demonstrates that a `bar.sync` without the proxy fence is not a valid substitute — the missing fence is a real, silicon-observable ordering hazard, not a theoretical one. (The divergence rate is low and timing-sensitive — inserting a per-launch sync often suppresses it — consistent with "the silicon usually drains fast enough, but the ISA ordering guarantee is genuinely absent and *is* occasionally violated under scheduling pressure.")
**Provenance.** Regression, introduced by [#2048](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/pull/2048) (`f11954cb`, "[Backend] Refactor gemm_sp", 2026-05-19), first shipped in **0.1.10**. Before #2048, the sparse sm90 path emitted the `call_intrin` `tl::tl_gemm_sp()`, which **is** in the `IsAsyncIntrinsic` list ([`inject_fence_proxy.cc:114`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/blob/cd37ed5fc35ae7a60a1277c8eb49028174ac51e6/src/cuda/transform/inject_fence_proxy.cc#L114)) — so sparse gemm **was** fenced at 0.1.9 (verified: `f11954cb^:src/backend/cuda/op/gemm_sp.cc:128` emits `tl::tl_gemm_sp()`). #2048 replaced that template path with direct `ptx_wgmma_sp_ss`/`ptx_wgmma_sp_rs` lowering and did **not** touch `inject_fence_proxy.cc` (git-verified via `--stat`), orphaning the fence and leaving the `tl_gemm_sp` list entry dead for the WGMMA path. The dense `ptx_wgmma_ss`/`ptx_wgmma_rs` entries were added earlier by #977; a later change (#1068) flipped the unlisted-intrinsic default from fail-safe (`kAsync`) toward fail-open, so an unlisted async intrinsic is no longer caught by default. On `main`, the `tl_gemm`/`tl_gemm_sp` fallbacks are removed entirely and the sparse variants are still absent — the defect persists. **Dedup.** I searched the open and closed tracker (`fence proxy`, `wgmma_sp fence`, `InjectFenceProxy`) and found no existing report. Distinct from the `cp.async.bulk`/cluster 16-byte-size and offset-alignment crash reports — those are alignment UB on the copy path; this is a missing proxy fence on the sparse WGMMA path.

title: [BUG][Fuzzer][ice-on-valid-code] Unary `+` on any expression (`+A[i]`) raises `TypeError` at trace time instead of compiling to the identity
body:
### Required prerequisites

- [x] I have read the documentation <https://tilelang.com>.
- [x] I have searched the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues) and no similar issue exists.

### What version of TileLang are you using?

0.1.13

### System information

NVIDIA L40S (sm_89) / CUDA 13.0 / PyTorch 2.13.0 / Python 3.13 — but the failure is target-independent: it fires at trace time, before any device code is generated.

### Problem description

A unary plus on a buffer element or any other expression — `Out[i] = +A[i]` — fails at trace time with `TypeError: bad operand type for unary +: 'BufferLoad'`, so a kernel using it never compiles. Unary minus (`-A[i]`), unary bitwise-not (`~A[i]`), and every binary operator on the same operand compile and run normally; only unary `+` is missing.

Unary `+` on a number is the identity operation in Python (`+5 == 5`, and `int`/`float`/`numpy` scalars all define it), so `+A[i]` is a well-formed expression a user can reasonably write — e.g. to mirror a reference formula or to make a sign explicit. The TVMScript operator registry even records the expectation that it is handled (`# doc.UAdd <-- is overloaded`), but the overload it relies on does not exist.

Both frontends are affected: the default eager `@tilelang.language` builder raises the raw `TypeError` above, and the classic `tvm.script` `@T.prim_func` parser surfaces the same Python exception through its diagnostic renderer (`error: bad operand type for unary +: 'BufferLoad'`). Not a regression — see Provenance.

### Reproducible example code

```python
import tilelang
import tilelang.language as T
import torch

# CONTROL: unary minus on a buffer element compiles and runs correctly.
@T.prim_func
def neg(A: T.Tensor((4,), "int32"), Out: T.Tensor((4,), "int32")):
    with T.Kernel(1, threads=1):
        for i in T.serial(4):
            Out[i] = -A[i]

k = tilelang.compile(neg, out_idx=[1])
a = torch.tensor([-5, 10, 0, 7], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
print(k(a).tolist())          # -> [5, -10, 0, -7]   (compiles, correct)

# TRIGGER: unary plus on the same element. Defining this prim_func alone
# raises at trace time (the @T.prim_func decorator traces eagerly):
@T.prim_func
def pos(A: T.Tensor((4,), "int32"), Out: T.Tensor((4,), "int32")):
    with T.Kernel(1, threads=1):
        for i in T.serial(4):
            Out[i] = +A[i]      # -> TypeError: bad operand type for unary +: 'BufferLoad'
```

### Traceback

```
  File ".../repro.py", line 9, in pos
    Out[i] = +A[i]
             ^^^^^
TypeError: bad operand type for unary +: 'BufferLoad'
```

### Expected behavior

`+A[i]` should compile and evaluate to the operand unchanged (identity), matching Python's numeric `__pos__` semantics and the fact that the sibling unary operators on the same expression type already work: `-A[i]` lowers to a multiply-by-`-1` and `~A[i]` to a bitwise-not. With a one-line `__pos__` added, `+A[i]` compiles and returns the input bit-for-bit for both integer and float buffers (verified below).

### Additional context

**Root cause.** The expression operator mixin `ExprOp` (in the vendored TVM under `3rdparty/tvm`, which every `PrimExpr` such as `BufferLoad` and `Var` inherits from) defines the full arithmetic/bitwise surface including `__neg__` and `__invert__` but never defines `__pos__`, so a Python unary `+` on any TileLang expression falls through to Python's default and raises `TypeError`. Both frontends route unary `+` straight to this operator: the classic parser's evaluator maps the AST node with `doc.UAdd: lambda a: +a`, and the TIR op registry leaves `UAdd` to Python overloading (`# doc.UAdd <-- is overloaded`) — but the overload it assumes is absent.

<details>
<summary>Source pointers and scope check</summary>

- [`ExprOp.__neg__`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/8df8ebd61659505dd7005f4820b030e983e2c005/python/tvm/tirx/expr.py#L123) and [`ExprOp.__invert__`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/8df8ebd61659505dd7005f4820b030e983e2c005/python/tvm/tirx/expr.py#L157) exist; there is no `__pos__` anywhere on the class (grep of `expr.py` finds 0 `__pos__`).
- classic parser: [`doc.UAdd: lambda a: +a`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/8df8ebd61659505dd7005f4820b030e983e2c005/python/tvm/script/parser/core/evaluator.py#L59)
- TIR op registry: [`# doc.UAdd <-- is overloaded`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/8df8ebd61659505dd7005f4820b030e983e2c005/python/tvm/tirx/script/parser/operation.py#L154-L155)

(The bundled TVM renamed `tir`→`tirx`, so `ExprOp` now lives at `python/tvm/tirx/expr.py`.)

The gap is `ExprOp`-wide, not buffer-specific — verified this session on v0.1.13, each in its own process:

| expression | `-` (neg) | `~` (invert) | `+` (pos) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A[i]` (int32 BufferLoad) | ok `[5,-10,0,-7]` | ok `[4,-11,-1,-8]` | crash `TypeError: bad operand type for unary +: 'BufferLoad'` |
| `A[i]` (float32 BufferLoad) | — | — | crash `TypeError: bad operand type for unary +: 'BufferLoad'` |
| `i` (bare loop `Var`) | — | — | crash `TypeError: bad operand type for unary +: 'Var'` |

Both `BufferLoad` and a bare `Var` fail identically, so the missing overload is on the shared `ExprOp` base, not on any one expression type. Class = **missing-case** (the `__pos__` method is absent from `ExprOp`); sibling unary operators `-`/`~` are present.
</details>

**Suggested fix.** Add a `__pos__` to `ExprOp` that returns the operand unchanged, e.g.

```python
def __pos__(self) -> PrimExpr:
    return self
```

<details>
<summary>Fix verified end-to-end (identity result on int and float)</summary>

With `ExprOp.__pos__ = lambda self: self` monkeypatched in (v0.1.13), the trigger kernel above compiles and runs, returning the input unchanged:

```
int32:   +A -> [-5, 10, 0, 7]           (== input, identity)   PASS
```
</details>

**Provenance.** The missing overload is long-standing: `ExprOp` ships without `__pos__` in the TVM fork pinned by TileLang 0.1.13 (`3rdparty/tvm` at `8df8ebd`, `python/tvm/tirx/expr.py` has `__neg__`/`__invert__` and zero `__pos__`), and upstream `apache/tvm` also has no `__pos__` on `ExprOp` (a code search finds `__neg__` in its `expr.py` but zero `__pos__`), so the gap predates the TileLang fork; an exact introducing commit was not traced.

**Generalization (tested this session, 0.1.13 / L40S).** The root is a missing `__pos__` on `ExprOp`, so the failure is *independent of dtype and expression shape* — anything Python routes to unary `+` on a PrimExpr fails, nothing else does. Tested (each fresh process): `+A[i]` (float32 load) → `TypeError: bad operand type for unary +: 'BufferLoad'`; `+A[i]` on an `int32` buffer → same `TypeError`; `+(A[i]*2.0)` (compound expression) → same. Control `-A[i]` (`__neg__`, which IS defined) → OK, `[-0,-1,-2,-3]`. So the boundary is exactly "unary `+` on any `PrimExpr`" — no dtype/shape knob changes it, because the operator is simply absent; the title is kept as the whole "unary `+` on any expression" class (already framed that way).

**Dedup.** I searched this project's filed issues and did not find an existing report of unary `+` / a missing `__pos__` overload; the closest, #2615, is a different mechanism (a Python builtin `min()` over `PrimExpr` operands, not a unary operator).

**Reach.** The trigger is a single unary `+` on a `PrimExpr` inside a `@T.prim_func`; it fires unconditionally, on any dtype and any target, the first time such an expression is traced (no shape/arch gate). A grep of the shipped package (220 `.py` files, excluding `3rdparty`) finds no unary-plus-on-expression site; the sibling unary operators `-`/`~` are the ones that appear in-tree, so no test exercises `+`.

**Impact.** The trigger is narrow but simple — any unary `+` on a traced expression, on any dtype/target. It is a trace-time `TypeError` (not a compiler abort and not a silent miscompile): it produces no wrong data and blocks only the one kernel from tracing, surfacing as an uncatchable Python exception raised eagerly at `@T.prim_func` decoration. A user mirroring a reference formula that writes `+x` hits a hard failure instead of the Python-standard identity.

**Distinctness.** This is a frontend `ExprOp.__pos__` gap — distinct root from the missing half-precision math lowering (`copysign`/`atan2`/`nextafter`) and from the `sync_global` backend `LOG(FATAL)`; kept as a specific report, not folded.

title: [Question][Carver] TensorCorePolicy: tiles whose smem_cost × pipeline_stage exceeds smem_cap are pruned rather than downgraded, and the shared.dyn fallback in _assign_block_size looks unreachable
body:
### Required prerequisites

- [x] I have read the documentation <https://tilelang.com>.
- [x] I have searched the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues) that this hasn't already been reported. (comment there if it has.)

### Questions

Two related observations in `tilelang/carver/roller/policy/` (line numbers identical on
`v0.1.13` and `main` @ `73bbff58`):

1. `TensorCorePolicy.infer_node_smem_usage` multiplies the shared-memory estimate by
   `self.pipeline_stage` (`tensorcore.py:83`). `DefaultPolicy.compute_tile_dict` then marks
   the tile invalid as soon as `td.smem_cost > self.arch.smem_cap` (`default.py:558-559`),
   and invalid tiles are filtered out of the search (`default.py:119`, `:132`). So a tile
   that would fit with `pipeline_stage = 1` but not with the arch-fixed `pipeline_stage = 2`
   is dropped entirely instead of being kept with a lower stage count. Is this pruning
   intended, or would a capacity-driven stage fallback (`max S s.t. S × smem_tile ≤ smem_cap`)
   be welcome? It mainly affects large tiles (e.g. fp16 128x256x32 at 2 stages is close to
   the 48 KB default `smem_cap`).

2. `_assign_block_size` (`tensorcore.py:328-333`) has a branch
   `if td.smem_cost > self.arch.smem_cap: shared_scope = "shared.dyn"`. Given (1), a tile
   reaching this point has already passed the same check, so the branch appears dead. It is
   then followed by an unconditional `codegen_dict.shared_scope = "shared.dyn"` (comment: a
   dummy to be removed), which also makes the earlier conditional assignment for
   `out_dtype == float32` (`:324`) dead. Is the unconditional `shared.dyn` meant to stay?

Asking before proposing a change: a stage fallback would touch the same lines, and the
answer to (2) decides whether it should also clean up the dead branches.

title: [BUG][Fuzzer][wrong-code] A loop `else:` clause (`for…else`/`while…else`) is silently dropped instead of executed or rejected
body:
### Required prerequisites - [x] I have read the documentation . - [x] I have searched the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues) and no similar issue was found. ### What version of TileLang are you using? 0.1.13 (latest release; also present on `main` at 6af825e). ### System information Python 3.13.13, linux tilelang 0.1.13 torch 2.13.0+cu130 GPU: NVIDIA L40S (sm_89) ### Problem description A `for … else:` (or `while … else:`) written inside a kernel compiles without any error, and the body of the `else:` clause is silently discarded — it never appears in the generated IR and never runs.
